title: Ferry Fare Change
story: You run the ticket window for a small river ferry. A crossing costs $5. Passengers pay with a single $5, $10 or $20 bill, and you must hand back exact change on the spot.

Your cash box starts empty in the morning. The only money you can give as change is the bills earlier passengers paid with. You know the order of today's passengers and the bill each will hand you. Can you serve all of them?
task: Write canGiveChange(bills). bills[i] is the bill the i-th passenger pays with, in queue order. Each passenger buys exactly one $5 ticket. Return true if you can give every passenger correct change, and false as soon as one passenger cannot get it.
Bills you receive go into the cash box and can be used as change for later passengers. An empty queue returns true.

examples.explanation: The first two passengers pay exactly: the box holds two $5. The third pays $10 and gets one $5 back: the box holds one $5 and one $10. The fourth pays $20 and needs $15: give the $10 and the $5. Everyone is served.
After the first two passengers, the box holds one $10 and no $5. The third passenger needs $5 back, and a $10 bill cannot be split. Fail.

hints: A $5 and a $10 are not equally useful as change. Which passengers can you serve with a $10 in the box, and which need a $5?
Every $10 passenger needs a $5 back. A $20 passenger needs $15, which is either $10 + $5 or $5 + $5 + $5. The $10 is only ever useful in that first combination.
When a $20 arrives and you could pay either way, which choice leaves you with more $5 bills for the passengers still to come?

Count $5 and $10 bills in the box (a $20 is never useful as change). For $10, give back a $5. For $20, prefer $10 + $5, and use three $5 bills only if you have no $10. Return false the moment a payment is impossible.
bruteForce: For every $20 passenger there are up to two ways to make change. You could try both ways for each of them and see if any sequence of choices serves the whole queue. With k passengers paying $20 that is up to 2k sequences, so 40 such passengers already means about a trillion tries.
The branching is wasted work: one of the two choices is never worse than the other, so you never need to try both.

js: * @return {boolean} true if every passenger gets exact change

tests.note: paying 20 with three 5s first fails later
long queue, fails near the end

js: let fives = 0, tens = 0; // $20 bills are never given as change
tens--; fives--; // spend the less useful $10 first
py: fives = tens = 0  # $20 bills are never given as change
tens -= 1  # spend the less useful $10 first
walkthrough: A $5 bill can help every future passenger. A $10 bill can only help a $20 passenger. So when you have a choice, spend the less flexible bill and keep the $5s.
• $20: you could give $10 + $5 or three $5s. Give $10 + $5. (2, 0).
Had you paid the $20 with three $5s, the box would hold (0, 1) and the last passenger could not get their $5. Same total money in the box, but the wrong shape.
solution.timeWhy: One pass over the queue, constant work per passenger.
solution.takeaway: When two choices meet today's need equally well, pick the one that keeps the most options open for later. Here that means spending the bill that can serve fewer future cases.
